chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ya'qub saying:

The meaning of His saying ('Recognize Allah through Allah') is that Allah, the Mighty and High, created persons, colors, and substances. Therefore, the essences are bodies and the substances are spirits. He, the Mighty and High, resembles neither body nor spirit. Nobody has any effect or cause in the creation of a sensitive, perceiving spirit. He is Matchless in the creation of spirits and bodies. Therefore, whoever negates from Him the two likenesses – the likeness of bodies and the likeness of spirits – recognizes Allah through Allah. And whoever views Him as a body, a spirit, or a light, has not recognized Allah through Allah.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to recognize Allah through Allah according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to articulate the Imami doctrine of divine transcendence (tanzih), distinguishing between the created categories of body (jism) and spirit (ruh) and the Uncreated Essence. By negating both physical form and immaterial essence from Allah, it refutes the Ghulat who attributed divinity to human figures, establishing that true recognition comes from understanding God's absolute uniqueness beyond all created modes of existence.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 5. `Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Imran al-Daqqaq (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Ya`qub said:

The meaning of” “recognize Allah through Allah” is that Allah, the Mighty and High, created persons, colors, and substances. Therefore, the essences are bodies and the substances are spirits. He, the Mighty and High, resembles neither body nor spirit. Nobody has any effect or cause in creation of a sensitive, perceiving spirit. He is Matchless in the creation of spirits, and bodies. Therefore, whoever negates from Him the two likenesses – the likeness of bodies and the likeness of spirits – recognizes Allah through Allah. And whoever views Him as a body, a spirit or a light, has not recognized Allah through Allah.
